paragraphs: AC contains doxorubicin and cyclophosphamide. Chemotherapy can lower infection-fighting white blood cells, which can allow an infection to become serious.
objects.title: Why it matters with this treatment

paragraphs: Diarrhea can occur with capecitabine. Ongoing diarrhea can cause loss of fluid and body salts.
objects.title: Why it matters with this treatment

paragraphs: Diarrhea means loose, watery, or unformed bowel movements, or going more often than is usual for you. It may come with urgency, bloating, or cramps.
Other conditions can cause similar symptoms. Ariad cannot determine the cause.
objects.title: About this symptom

bullets: There are more than seven loose or watery bowel movements in 24 hours.
Diarrhea continues for more than 24 hours after medicine used according to your team's instructions.
You cannot drink enough, there is blood, or you have belly pain other than your usual cramping.
You notice thirst, dry mouth, dark or reduced urine, dizziness, vomiting, or a fast heartbeat.
objects.title: Contact your cancer team if…

bullets: Keep a record of bowel movements.
Unless your team has limited your fluids, sip fluids regularly.
Choose small meals and limit caffeine, alcohol, spicy foods, and high-fat foods.
Use anti-diarrheal medicine only as your cancer team instructed.
Keep the skin around the anus clean and dry, and use gentle care after bowel movements.
paragraphs: These are general measures. Follow any fluid, diet, or medicine instructions provided by your cancer team.
objects.title: What you can generally do at home

bullets: When the diarrhea began and the number of loose or watery bowel movements in 24 hours.
How that compares with your usual bowel pattern, including nighttime episodes.
Any blood, mucus, vomiting, dizziness, belly pain, or measured temperature.
How much you have been able to drink and any change in urination.
Any anti-diarrheal medicine used according to your team's instructions and your last capecitabine dose.
objects.title: What information to have ready

bullets: You cannot reach your cancer team and have the warning signs listed above.
You think this may be a medical emergency.
paragraphs: This prototype does not provide a local fever threshold. Follow the fever instructions provided by your cancer team.
placeholders: clinic-specific fever threshold pending clinician review
objects.title: Seek urgent medical attention if…

paragraphs: Fever, chills, or feeling unwell can be signs of infection. Infection can sometimes occur without a fever.
Ariad cannot diagnose an infection or tell whether white blood cells are low.
objects.title: About this symptom

bullets: You have chills, shaking, sweats, a sore throat, or a cough.
You have burning or blood with urination, mouth sores, or redness or tenderness around a wound or line.
You have uncontrolled vomiting or diarrhea.
You feel unwell even without a measured fever.
objects.title: Contact your cancer team if…

bullets: Keep a working digital thermometer available.
If you feel hot, chilled, or unwell, take your temperature before using fever-reducing medicine, because that medicine can hide a fever.
Avoid hot or cold food and drink immediately before an oral temperature measurement.
Wash your hands often and keep cuts or line sites clean.
paragraphs: Follow the infection and fever instructions provided by your cancer team.
objects.title: What you can generally do at home

bullets: Your highest temperature, how it was measured, and the times it was measured.
Any chills, shaking, sweats, cough, sore throat, breathing, urinary, bowel, mouth, skin, or line symptoms.
When AC was last given.
Whether fever-reducing medicine was taken and when.
objects.title: What information to have ready

bullets: You cannot reach your cancer team and feel acutely unwell.
You have shortness of breath, faintness, marked dizziness, or a fast heartbeat.
You think this may be a medical emergency.
paragraphs: This prototype does not provide a local fever threshold. Follow the fever instructions provided by your cancer team.
placeholders: clinic-specific fever threshold and destination pending clinician review
objects.title: Seek urgent medical attention if…

paragraphs: Peripheral neuropathy can feel like tingling, pins and needles, numbness, burning, or pain, often in the fingers or toes. It can also affect grip, balance, or movement.
Other conditions can cause similar symptoms. Ariad cannot determine the cause.
objects.title: About this symptom

bullets: You notice new tingling, numbness, burning, pain, or weakness.
Symptoms are worsening or spreading.
Symptoms interfere with buttons, writing, holding objects, walking, or balance.
objects.title: Contact your cancer team if…

bullets: Protect areas with reduced feeling and check your hands and feet for cuts.
Use supportive shoes and protective gloves for household or outdoor tasks.
Test bath water with your elbow before putting numb hands or feet into it.
Keep floors and walkways well lit and clear of clutter.
Ask your team about driving if sensation or foot control is affected.
paragraphs: These are general precautions. Follow the instructions provided by your cancer team.
objects.title: What you can generally do at home

bullets: Where the sensation is and whether it is tingling, numbness, burning, or pain.
When it began and whether it is changing.
Effects on buttons, writing, small objects, walking, or balance.
Any weakness, falls, near-falls, burns, cuts, or other injuries.
Your treatment name and the date of your last treatment.
objects.title: What information to have ready

bullets: You develop sudden confusion or trouble speaking.
You have sudden difficulty moving an arm or leg.
You have a seizure or pass out.
paragraphs: These are general neurological emergency signs. They do not identify or grade peripheral neuropathy.
objects.title: Seek urgent medical attention if…

paragraphs: Peripheral neuropathy can occur with paclitaxel. Symptoms may affect tasks such as fastening buttons, writing, or picking up small objects.
objects.title: Why it matters with this treatment

paragraphs: Weekly paclitaxel is a breast-cancer chemotherapy regimen using paclitaxel, a taxane medicine given through a vein.
Your own schedule and instructions come from your cancer team.
objects.title: Your treatment at a glance

bullets: Tiredness, nausea, and hair loss can occur.
Lowered blood counts and infection concerns can occur.
Tingling, numbness, burning, or pain in the hands or feet can occur.
paragraphs: Paclitaxel can be associated with several effects. Your experience may differ, and this prototype cannot predict which effects you will have.
objects.title: Effects to know about

bullets: Save your cancer team's daytime and after-hours contact information.
Keep a working digital thermometer available and follow your team's fever instructions.
Bring an up-to-date medication list and follow only the medicine instructions your team provided.
Know how to reach your treatment area if you have questions before a visit.
objects.title: A simple preparation checklist

paragraphs: Ariad can show source-controlled warning information, but it cannot decide whether a symptom is caused by treatment or tell you what action you personally need.
Follow the instructions provided by your cancer team. If you think you may be experiencing a medical emergency, call 911 or your local emergency service.
